title: Implement ?ping= query parameter on /jmap/events (RFC 8620 §7.3)
description:
What: /jmap/events must honour a ?ping=N query parameter (N = integer seconds) per RFC 8620 §7.3. When present, send a ping SSE event every N seconds. Currently EventsQuery has only 'types' and 'closeafter'.

Algorithm:
1. Read kithd/src/events.rs in full; locate EventsQuery struct and the axum handler
2. Add field to EventsQuery:
   ping: Option<u64>
3. Validate ping on receipt:
   - If present but not parseable as integer: return 400 Bad Request
   - If 0: treat as None (no ping)
   - If > 300: cap at 300 (reasonable max; document in comment)
4. Pass ping_secs to KeepAlive:
   - If ping_secs.is_some(): Sse::new(stream).keep_alive(KeepAlive::new().interval(Duration::from_secs(ping_secs)))
   - If None: Sse::new(stream).keep_alive(KeepAlive::new().interval(Duration::from_secs(30))) [current default]
5. KeepAlive sends a comment ping ('': '') — RFC 8620 §7.3 says a ping event with {"interval":N} must also be sent on first connect. Add that: send a synthetic Event::default().event("ping").data(json!({"interval":ping_secs}).to_string()) as the first item in the stream before the coalescing channel output.
6. For closeafter: if present, start a timeout task that closes the stream after N seconds (axum SSE stream ends when sender drops)

Defensive programming rules:
- Reject non-integer ping values with 400 before entering the SSE handler
- Cap ping at 300s; never allow 0 as a live interval (SSE flood risk)
- The ping event must be the FIRST event on the stream so the client knows the server's interval
- closeafter timeout: use tokio::time::sleep in a spawned task that drops the tx; do not block the handler
- Do not change the coalescing logic or the 'state' event format

Agent team: R+I+T agent (kithd/src/events.rs only)

Tests:
- Unit test: parse_ping_param_rejects_non_integer — assert 400 for '?ping=abc'
- Unit test: parse_ping_param_caps_at_300 — assert ping=999 results in effective 300
- Unit test: ping_event_is_first_on_stream — synthetic ping event precedes any state events
- cargo test -p kithd passes (all 48+ existing tests unchanged)
